[1/4] Plan: append-only hash-chained Merkle batch journal with historical proofs

impact_assessment.why: The single .merkle sidecar is overwritten by each new anchor, so an earlier batch root and its inclusion proofs are lost. The telemetry anchor journal solved the same overwrite problem for head anchors.
impact_assessment.benefits: append_merkle_anchor appends batches with prev/hash links and monotonic ranges; verify_merkle_journal names prev/order/root/truncation defects; merkle_proof_for_journal_record proves membership in an earlier batch after a newer anchor is written; the single-anchor API is unchanged.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new journal functions/wrappers; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: single-writer append under fsync (same boundary as the single anchor); state: new .merkle.journal sidecar, not committed.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep the single-anchor format untouched; validate every record's schema/ranges/root/prev/hash; reject range rollback; test intact, truncated, deleted, tampered, rollback, missing and proof cases; run 266 tests and AIKit.

[1/4] Plan: skip backend calls after 3 consecutive progress rejections

impact_assessment.why: The cycle-72 progress guard still calls the backend every step: a wrong-way backend costs 13/6/8 calls on T3:15/T3:65/T2:3 for 12/5/8 rejections, so repeated wrong-way proposals keep spending model budget.
impact_assessment.benefits: After three consecutive progress rejections the planner returns the rule action without calling the backend (reason skipped-progress); calls fall 13/6/8 -> 4/4/3 while steps/rewards stay 13/6/8 and 1.0; T1 stays 36/22.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: Planner progress_skip_after keyword and policy key (policy digest changes); dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: none; state: no schema change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Count only consecutive progress rejections, reset the streak on every non-progress outcome and per episode; keep progress_skip_after=None for the guard-only ablation; test skip-on/None/alternating/reset/invalid and rerun 282 tests plus AIKit.

[1/4] Plan: durable checksummed claim-ledger store with backup and quarantine recovery

impact_assessment.why: ClaimLedger roundtrips as JSON but has no file API, so verdicts and kill-test evidence are lost when the process exits. The open-ended evidence loop needs a durable claim store.
impact_assessment.benefits: save_ledger writes one checksummed snapshot atomically (temp+fsync+replace) with a .bak of the previous snapshot; load_ledger restores it, quarantines a corrupt primary and falls back to .bak; verify_ledger_file names missing/checksum/schema defects; a lock serialises writers and steals stale locks.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new claims_store.py module only, no agent API change; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: O_CREAT|O_EXCL lock with 30s stale steal and bounded timeout; state: new local snapshot/.bak/.lock files, not committed.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep ClaimLedger as the data model; verify schema/checksum/claims on load; write temp+fsync+replace with 5 retries and a .bak; test roundtrip, backup fallback, tamper, schema, stale lock, fresh-lock timeout, deterministic checksum and no temp leftovers; rerun 282 tests and AIKit.
